324.h: Skyline University Nigeria (SUN) is a private university that received Federal Government approval in May 2018. It was the first private university in Kano and the second in north-western Nigeria.
324.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
324.c: It is located in Kano, the capital of Kano State.

325.h: Sokoto State University (SSU) is a public university owned by the Sokoto State Government. It was established in 2009 under the administration of Governor Aliyu Wamakko.
325.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
325.c: It is located in Sokoto, the capital of Sokoto State in north-western Nigeria.

326.h: Sule Lamido University is a public university owned by the Jigawa State Government. It was established on 13 May 2013 and licensed by the National Universities Commission in July 2013 as Jigawa State University. Teaching began in September 2014, and in December 2014 a law passed by the Jigawa State House of Assembly renamed it after Sule Lamido, the governor at the time.
326.c: It is located in Kafin Hausa, Jigawa State.

327.h: Summit University, Offa is a private university founded in 2015 by the Ansar-Ud-Deen Society of Nigeria, a Muslim organisation devoted to education. It was one of ten private universities licensed in Nigeria that year, and one of the few private universities in Kwara State.
327.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
327.c: It is located in Offa, Kwara State, in north-central Nigeria.

328.h: Tai Solarin Federal University of Education (TASUED) is a university dedicated to teacher education, named after Tai Solarin, the educationist and social critic. It began as Tai Solarin University of Education, owned by the Ogun State Government, and the National Universities Commission lists it as a federal university of education from 2025.
328.a: The university has grown from four colleges to six. It was the first Nigerian university to have a full college dedicated to vocational and technology education, which trains teachers for technical and vocational subjects.
328.c: The campus is at Ijagun, near Ijebu-Ode, in Ogun State.

329.h: Tansian University (TANU) is a private Christian university founded by John Bosco Akam. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2007. It began on a temporary site at Oba, in Idemili South, before moving to its permanent site.
329.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
329.c: Its permanent campus is at Umunya, in Oyi local government area of Anambra State.

330.h: Taraba State University (TSU) is a public university established by the Taraba State Government in 2008 to widen access to university education and support development in the state.
330.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
330.c: It is located in Jalingo, the capital of Taraba State.

331.h: Umaru Musa Yar'Adua University (UMYU) is a public university founded in 2006 by the Katsina State Government as Katsina State University. It was later renamed after Umaru Musa Yar'Adua, a former governor of Katsina State who became President of Nigeria. It was set up to drive the state's development by training skilled graduates and producing research.
331.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
331.c: It is located in Katsina, the capital of Katsina State.

332.h: The University of Abuja is a federal university established in January 1988 as a dual-mode university, with a mandate to run both conventional and distance-learning programmes. Teaching began in 1990 with the matriculation of its pioneer students. On 16 December 2024 President Bola Tinubu renamed it Yakubu Gowon University, in honour of the former head of state on his 90th birthday.
332.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in most fields, including medicine, and runs distance-learning programmes alongside conventional ones.
332.c: It is located in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

333.h: University of Africa, Toru-Orua (UAT) is a public university owned by the Bayelsa State Government. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2016, while the university itself dates its start to 2017.
333.c: It is located at Toru-Orua in Sagbama local government area, Bayelsa State.

334.h: The University of Benin (UNIBEN) is a federal university founded in 1970. It is one of Nigeria's older federal universities and one of the largest in the south of the country.
334.a: UNIBEN is organised into faculties, each with several departments, and departments run one or more degree programmes. Most undergraduate programmes take four to six years, depending on the course and the mode of entry. The university offers a wide range of programmes, including medicine, engineering, law, pharmacy and the arts and sciences.
334.c: The university is in Benin City, the capital of Edo State.

335.h: The University of Calabar (UNICAL) is a federal university and one of Nigeria's second-generation federal universities. It was a campus of the University of Nigeria until 1975, when it became an independent university. Its motto is 'Knowledge for Service', and its buildings were designed by the architect John Elliott.
335.a: UNICAL offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in most disciplines, including medicine.
335.c: The university is in Calabar, the capital of Cross River State.

336.h: The University of Fortune (UF) is a private university that was licensed by the Federal Government in April 2025, though work on it began several years earlier, with its foundation laid in 2020.
336.a: As one of Nigeria's newest universities, it offers an initial range of undergraduate programmes.
336.c: It is located in Igbotako, in Okitipupa local government area of Ondo State.

337.h: The University of Ilorin (UNILORIN) is a federal public research university, established by decree of the Federal Military Government in August 1975.
337.a: UNILORIN has 16 faculties and more than 100 academic departments offering 103 programmes. It enrols more international students than any other Nigerian university.
337.c: The main campus in Ilorin, Kwara State, covers about 5,000 hectares, making it the largest university campus in Nigeria by land area and one of the largest in Africa.

338.h: The University of Jos (UNIJOS) is a federal university established in 1975. It began as a campus of the University of Ibadan before becoming an independent university.
338.a: UNIJOS offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in most disciplines, including medicine.
338.c: The university is in Jos, the capital of Plateau State, on the Jos Plateau in central Nigeria.

339.h: The University of Maiduguri (UNIMAID), now named Muhammadu Buhari University, is a federal university established in 1975, one of the group of universities the Federal Government founded that year.
339.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in most disciplines, including medicine, and is one of the major universities of north-eastern Nigeria.
339.c: It is located in Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State.

340.h: The University of Mkar is a private faith-based university founded in 2005 by the Universal Reformed Christian Church, known in Tiv as Nongu u Kristu u i Ser sha Tar (NKST).
340.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
340.c: It is located in Mkar, near Gboko, in Benue State.

342.h: The University of Port Harcourt (UNIPORT) is a public research university. It was established in 1975 as University College, Port Harcourt, and gained full university status in 1977. In 2015 Times Higher Education ranked it first in Nigeria and sixth in Africa.
342.a: UNIPORT offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across most disciplines, with notable strengths in engineering, geosciences and medicine.
342.c: The campus lies at Aluu and Choba, on the outskirts of Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

343.h: The University of Uyo (UNIUYO) is a federal university. It took over the students, staff, programmes and facilities of the University of Cross River State, which the state had established in 1983. On 1 October 1991 the Federal Government made it a federal university and renamed it the University of Uyo. The institution itself grew in stages from a teachers' college.
343.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine.
343.c: It is located in Uyo, the capital of Akwa Ibom State.

344.h: Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS) is a public research university, one of the universities the Federal Government founded in 1975. It is named after Usman dan Fodio, the nineteenth-century scholar and reformer who founded the Sokoto Caliphate.
344.a: UDUS offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine, and is a leading centre for Islamic studies and agricultural research in north-western Nigeria.
344.c: The university is located in the city of Sokoto, in north-western Nigeria.

345.h: Veritas University is the private university of the Catholic Church in Nigeria, founded by the Catholic Bishops' Conference in March 2002. It received its provisional licence from the National Universities Commission in 2007 and admitted its first students in October 2008 at a temporary campus in Obehie, Abia State, before moving to Abuja.
345.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. Its software engineering lab won the 3rd African Telecommunications Union Africa Innovation Challenge, which carried a prize of US$20,000.
345.c: The university is located in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

346.h: Wellspring University is a private university licensed by the Federal Government in November 2009. It was founded by the Management Science Centre, a professional training and education consulting firm set up in 1983, and is based on Christian principles.
346.a: Undergraduate programmes are run in four colleges, and postgraduate programmes in a postgraduate school. All academic programmes are accredited by the National Universities Commission.
346.c: It is located in Benin City, Edo State.

347.h: Western Delta University (WDU) is a private university established in 2007 by a group of Urhobo scholars through the Urhobo Advancement Foundation. They saw the need for a privately funded university in the wetlands of Delta State.
347.a: The university offers a range of undergraduate programmes.
347.c: It is located at Unoghovo-Oghara, Delta State.

348.h: Yobe State University (YSU) is a public university owned by the Yobe State Government. It was established under a state law in 2006 by Bukar Abba Ibrahim, executive governor of Yobe State from 1999 to 2007.
348.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
348.c: It is located in Damaturu, the capital of Yobe State.
